item.title: Employee Rights Weekly: November 9 through November 15, 2026
item.description:
Added to this feed on November 21, 2026, as a back episode. Coverage reflects what we could confirm from official and reputable sources.

Coverage: November 9 through November 15, 2026

Eleventh Circuit

Nothing new confirmed this week.

Florida Appellate Courts

Nothing new confirmed this week.

EEOC

  • Wabash National Settles EEOC Pregnancy Discrimination Lawsuit, EEOC, Nov. 13, 2026. Resolves the EEOC's first PWFA lawsuit: $50,000 and a two-year consent decree with nationwide policy and training obligations; alleged denial of a transfer accommodation and forced unpaid leave. Source
  • A.W. Farrell & Son to Pay $270,000 in EEOC Sex Discrimination Lawsuit, EEOC, Nov. 10, 2026. Same-sex harassment of a male roofer by his supervisor, alleged to have forced his resignation. Source

Department of Labor

Nothing new confirmed this week.

NLRB

Nothing new confirmed this week.

Three things to watch

  1. Ask pregnant clients whether they requested a transfer or change in duties.
  2. Consider pleading PWFA claims alongside Title VII and the ADA.
  3. Evaluate constructive discharge before treating a harassment-driven resignation as voluntary.

item.title: Employee Rights Weekly: November 2 through November 8, 2026
item.description:
Added to this feed on November 21, 2026, as a back episode. Coverage reflects what we could confirm from official and reputable sources.

Coverage: November 2 through November 8, 2026

Eleventh Circuit

  • Rasberry v. Secretary of the Navy, 11th Cir., unpublished, Nov. 5, 2026, No. 25-14381. Affirmed summary judgment on a federal-sector Title VII retaliation claim; the plaintiff failed to show retaliation played any part in an adverse action. Source

Florida Appellate Courts

Nothing new confirmed this week.

EEOC

  • Gator Strong Services Resolves EEOC Sexual Harassment Suit, EEOC, Nov. 2, 2026. $25,000 under a two-year consent decree; alleged harassment by a former COO and firing of an office manager. Source
  • Mid-Michigan Home Health & Hospice to Pay $41,137, EEOC, Nov. 3, 2026. Race discrimination and retaliation; alleged firing within 48 hours of a complaint about assignments. Source

Department of Labor

Nothing new confirmed this week.

NLRB

Nothing new confirmed this week.

Three things to watch

  1. Identify the actual decision maker in every retaliation case and pin down what they knew and when.
  2. Scrutinize the timing of discipline relative to protected activity.
  3. For clients at small employers, an EEOC charge remains a practical path to relief.

Created with AI. Not legal advice. Check every source before relying on it.

item.title: Employee Rights Weekly: October 26 through November 1, 2026
item.description:
Added to this feed on November 21, 2026, as a back episode. Coverage reflects what we could confirm from official and reputable sources.

Coverage: October 26 through November 1, 2026

Eleventh Circuit

Nothing new confirmed this week.

Florida Appellate Courts

Nothing new confirmed this week.

EEOC

  • EEOC Votes to Rescind Enforcement Guidance on Arrest and Conviction Records, EEOC, press release Oct. 29, 2026. Rescinds the 2012 Title VII guidance, effective immediately; does not restore superseded policy statements or require employers to drop lawful practices. Source
  • Smithfield Fresh Meats Corp. to Pay $245,000 in EEOC Pregnancy Discrimination Suit, EEOC, Oct. 29, 2026. Settles claims that the company denied pregnancy accommodation, forced unpaid leave, and fired the employee. Source

Department of Labor

  • Pharmacy benefit manager fee disclosure final rule, DOL Employee Benefits Security Administration, late October 2026. Requires PBMs and affiliated brokers and consultants to disclose fees and compensation to fiduciaries of large self-insured group health plans under ERISA. Source

NLRB

Nothing new confirmed this week.

Three things to watch

  1. Re-examine background check cases now that the EEOC guidance is rescinded; rely on Title VII, case law, and state or local law.
  2. In pregnancy cases, look for forced unpaid leave instead of a workable accommodation.
  3. Watch the new PBM disclosures as possible evidence in ERISA health plan fiduciary claims.

Created with AI. Not legal advice. Check every source before relying on it.

item.title: Employee Rights Weekly: October 19 through October 25, 2026
item.description:
Added to this feed on November 21, 2026, as a back episode. Coverage reflects what we could confirm from official and reputable sources.

Coverage: October 19 through October 25, 2026

Eleventh Circuit

  • Holland v. 3M Company, 11th Cir., unpublished, Oct. 20, 2026, No. 25-13734. Affirmed summary judgment for 3M on a Title VII religious discrimination claim; the district court found no conflict between the employee's stated religious beliefs and 3M's policies. Source

Florida Appellate Courts

Nothing new confirmed this week.

EEOC

  • EEOC Sues Solera Holdings for Disability Discrimination, EEOC, Oct. 20, 2026. ADA suit alleging the company denied a blind employee the same job support and resources given to coworkers, then fired him. Source

Department of Labor

  • Field Assistance Bulletin No. 2026-1, DOL Wage and Hour Division, Oct. 19, 2026. Withdraws three older opinion letters on related duties performed by tipped employees under the FLSA. Source
  • Overtime recoveries: New Jersey drywall installer ($725,000, 48 workers, Oct. 19) and Indiana auto parts maker ($603,953, 829 workers, Oct. 22), DOL Wage and Hour Division. Consent judgment and investigation recoveries for overtime violations. Source

NLRB

  • Supreme Court declines review of Wilcox removal case, U.S. Supreme Court, Oct. 19, 2026. Leaves in place the D.C. Circuit ruling that the President may remove NLRB members at will. Source

Three things to watch

  1. Check whether any DOL letter you rely on in tip credit cases was withdrawn by FAB 2026-1.
  2. In religious accommodation cases, document the specific conflict between belief and job requirement early.
  3. Expect NLRB precedent to change faster; factor that into advice on NLRA claims.

Created with AI. Not legal advice. Check every source before relying on it.
